status: Draft from the mishnah, R. Kulp and Kehati.

principles.t: An owner who guarded his flock properly is exempt if it escapes through no fault; one who did not is liable.
A flock that falls into a garden pays what it benefited; one that enters normally pays the damage, assessed by the value of a seah's space.
Whoever kindles a fire (esh) pays for everything it burns. When several contribute, the last one is liable; a wind frees all only if it was unusual.
The distance a fire must travel to be exempt is disputed; the halakha follows Rabbi Shimon, by the nature of the fire.
The Sages: goods are paid for only where it is customary to keep them (a building, not a stack of hay); Rabbi Judah: he pays for all that was in it.

terms.def: The fourth archetypal cause of damage: the one who kindles a fire pays for the damage it does.
Damage caused indirectly, such as bandits who break a pen and the flock then leaves. Not liable in human law.

terms.term: laws of man and of Heaven
terms.def: A wrong that cannot be prosecuted in court but for which the person is still accountable.

debates.title: How far must the fire spread?
debates.a: Rabbi Eleazar ben Azariah: like the middle of a kor's space; Rabbi Eliezer: 16 cubits; Rabbi Akiva: 50.
debates.b: All by the nature of the fire. The halakha follows this view.
debates.wa: R. Eleazar ben Azariah / R. Eliezer / R. Akiva

debates.title: Utensils inside a stack that burned
debates.a: He pays for what was in it.
debates.b: Only for the wheat or barley. In a large building all agree he pays for the contents.

debates.title: The Hanukkah light outside the shop
debates.a: The shopkeeper who left his light outside is liable.
debates.b: Not liable for a Hanukkah light. The halakha does not follow him.
